method: Small mathematical application of old exact singleton inventories; no new native query, phoneme mapping, language score or experiment.
premises: Each admitted whole output group is one complete lexical source word.
Every source letter has one fixed nonempty written code; ordinary concatenation, no zero-output source letters, code overlap or multiple spellings for a source letter.
Every lexical source word contains at least one source letter from an independently specified vowel-letter set V.
Keep all original22-working-unit and strict internal definite-space assumptions; raw readers remain separate.
proof: A one-working-unit complete group can contain exactly one nonempty source-letter code, hence represents a one-letter source word.
By the declared lexical-source condition this source letter must belong to V.
Different singleton output forms require different source letters when every source letter has exactly one fixed spelling.
Therefore |V| is at least the number of distinct singleton complete forms, separately for each reading.
not_established: No source language actually has at most six vowels here; six is an explicit model example, not an observed Voynich fact.
Vowel LETTERS are not vowel sounds; no native glyph is classified as a vowel.
No general ban on alphabetic writing, vowel omission, syllabic scripts, abbreviations, numbers or contextual/allographic systems.
Rare source types remain in the old counts; no independent image confirmation is added.
Exceptions are obligations for a different fixed source contract, not permission to relabel awkward native groups after seeing them.
decoder_caution: For1253, physical xy is decoded as B, not Xx Xy. A vowel requirement must apply to the decoded source; a hitting set over raw output glyphs is not equivalent. Singleton groups are unaffected by this distinction.
decision: No cipher or raw-vowel-cover search for the strict <=6-vowel, word-preserving fixed-spelling class. A different complete source/word/abbreviation contract needs its own independent justification;1253formalcover remains supported.
